22605-book-lovers-bibliomaniacs-and-book:
Book Lovers, Bibliomaniacs and Book Clubs is an essay collection about the love of books and the people who collect them. The catalog record names no author and gives no year. It traces how book collecting, once a hobby of the rich, spread to people of moderate means.

Each generation of collectors, the author notes, has outnumbered the one before in both numbers and enthusiasm. The love of books creeps quietly into homes grand and humble, since a library counts as equipment for the mind as much as for the house. Clubs, sales, and famous collections fill the pages. The book is a friendly tour of bibliophile culture, written for readers who already suspect books are more than objects.
a-collection-of-scotch-proverbs: Pappity Stampoy gathered the shrewd, funny sayings of the Scottish folk — proverbs on thrift, weather, neighbors, and human folly. Each one packs a lifetime of canny wisdom into a line or two. A merry, wise book that lets readers hear the voice of old Scotland.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-caribs: This 1913 reference piece on the Caribs — the island warriors. Adolph Francis Bandelier surveys their customs and faith. The missionaries braved their fierce shores. The islands knew their bold canoes. A people of the Caribbean sea. Their Dominica island is the last refuge.

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-roman-catacom: The Roman Catacombs are the underground cities of the martyrs. This long entry treats their galleries, their art, and their discovery. The sleeping-places of the saints: their faded frescoes guard the faith of the martyrs in the dark below Rome.

podcast-dannyjones-IMFvB1_2wbs:
Geologist Randall Carlson and researcher Ben Van Kerkwyk join Danny Jones to explore ancient earth's most violent catastrophes. They discuss impacts, floods, and firestorms. In their account, such events smashed early human civilization and were remembered worldwide as myth.

Randall Carlson has argued for decades that a comet strike reset human history at the end of the last ice age. Mainstream geology has partly warmed to that claim and partly resisted it. Van Kerkwyk adds the field evidence from sites they have visited together. Jones plays the informed amateur, asking for the strongest proofs. The episode is a seminar in catastrophism from its leading popularizers. Listeners can follow the geological argument in detail and judge where it converges with, and where it departs from, the textbooks.
podcast-joerogan-hwRD0NvAnbs:
Paul Stamets is back with Rogan for episode 2347 of the Joe Rogan Experience, with more mushrooms in hand. Stamets, the mycologist who never tires of his subject, treats each visit as a new dispatch from the fungal world. His enthusiasm is the show's renewable resource.

He and Rogan range across mycelium networks, mushroom medicine, and the mind-bending finds his field keeps producing. Rogan feeds him the questions of a fascinated amateur. The episode is a feast for the myco-curious, proof that one man's life work, retold with joy, can hold an audience through many returns to the same rich ground.

tanakh-jps-1917-proverbs: Short, sharp sayings about how to live well: work hard, speak carefully, avoid fools, honor your parents. Most are credited to Solomon, famed for wisdom. This 1917 Jewish Publication Society edition collects the Bible's practical wisdom in the first English translation by Jewish scholars.
the-book-of-snobs: Thackeray's 1848 Book of Snobs: the anatomy of snobbery in all its forms. "Snobs are to be studied like other objects of Natural Science." The wittiest social satire in English. Thackeray's snobs are eternal and everywhere, the funniest anatomy of folly.
